work: Bar do thos grol chen mo: texts kha and ga of BDRC W23710
notes: Cut by pages of the reproduction, about nine to a part (the pilot's size): pages 18–121, the pilot (bardo-thodol-001) having covered pp. 9–17 to the words ...yid la 'jags su bcug go༔. Page p is leaf n(p+1) of the scan; images in source/pages/n<leaf>.jpg (the scan's 3000-px images, native 2021×494). Leaf n80 carries both page numbers 79 and 80 (the last page of text kha); leaf n81 is blank.

Text kha (the Chos nyid bar do'i gsal 'debs, the peaceful deities) ends on leaf n80 (p. 79/80). Text ga begins with its title leaf, p. 81 (n82: ཁྲོ་བོའི་བར་དོ་འཆར་ཚུལ་བསྟན་པ་བཞུགས་སོ, as first read in setup; the establishing firing reads it exactly), and ends on p. 121/122 (n122). p. 123 (n124) is the title of the next text of the cycle, not on this list (see QUESTIONS.md).

A part's text is established in its own firing: it begins exactly where the previous part's established text ends and runs to the last ༔ (or ། ) that closes a sentence on its last page; a sentence running over the page edge is finished from the next page — except at the end of a text (p. 80, p. 121), where the part ends with the text. The establishing firing names the part. The first part of text ga (bardo-thodol-009) begins with its title leaf as its own heading unit.
